name: Muhammad
role: Prophet of Islam; founder and ruler of the Medinan state (c. 571-632)
summary: Muhammad proclaimed the Quran as divine revelation and led the community in Medina as religious teacher, lawgiver, judge and military commander. His recorded positions combine religious law, mutual defence and welfare duties such as zakat with a ban on interest. He ruled through a covenant that included Jewish tribes as allies, and later expelled or fought some of them.

reviewHistory.rationale: Watt (Muhammad at Medina, pp. 228-229) records that he could not act directly against his Medinan opponent Ibn Ubayy, who was left unpunished, while at Mecca he ordered a few opponents killed even if found under the curtains of the Ka'ba (Ibn Ishaq, p. 550); the record points both ways.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: He had Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf killed for having 'hurt Allah and His Apostle' (Bukhari 4037) and ordered Ibn Khatal's singing-girls, who sang satires about him, killed (Ibn Ishaq, p. 551), yet his covenant let the Jewish clans keep their religion (p. 233): insult punished, other scriptural religions tolerated.

reviewHistory.rationale: Contested: Quran 6:108 tells believers not to revile what others invoke, but 9:12 threatens treaty-breakers who defame the religion, and the Mecca account records some who insulted him being excluded from the amnesty.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Quran 2:190 and 22:39 permit fighting those who fight or wrong the believers, and 9:38-39 rebukes those who do not go forth when called; an obligation on every Muslim is stated only for mobilisations he called.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Contested: Quran 5:44 calls those who do not judge by revelation disbelievers, but Bukhari 7056 permits resistance only for clear disbelief, and Muslim reports obeying rulers who still pray.

assisted-dying.rationale: He told of a man who, impatient with the pain of a wound, cut his hand until he died, and of God forbidding him Paradise for hastening his death (Bukhari 3463).

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Quran 12:40: "Legislation is not but for Allah"; 4:59 ties obedience to those in authority to obedience to Allah and the Messenger.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Watt (Muhammad at Medina, pp. 231-232 and the list of expeditions) records the forces he raised and led or sent out from Medina, from the first raids and Badr onward.

reviewHistory.rationale: He maintained an army in Medina and Quran 8:60 tells believers to prepare all the force they can.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Quran 2:221 forbids marrying polytheists, while 5:5 permits marrying chaste women of the People of the Book; marriage across religions is partly restricted.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Contested: Quran praises private giving (2:261), yet 9:103 and 9:60 set a collected, officially administered zakat for the poor.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Quran 4:34 says men are in charge of women and 2:228 gives men a degree over them; in the Farewell Sermon he allowed husbands to confine and beat, 'but not with severity', wives guilty of open unseemliness (Ibn Ishaq, p. 651).

reviewHistory.rationale: Quran 4:34 says men are in charge of women, and 2:228 says men have a degree over them, alongside similar rights; the Farewell Sermon assigns the husband authority over household access.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Quran 22:39 permits fighting by those attacked; Bukhari 2480 reports him saying whoever is killed protecting his property is a martyr. He endorsed defensive killing.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Quran 4:76 says believers fight in the cause of God and unbelievers in the cause of false gods, and 58:19-22 sets the party of Satan against the party of God.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Quran 15:29 speaks of God breathing His spirit into the first human, and 2:201 asks for good in this world and in the Hereafter.

racial-pride.rationale: He said God had removed the pre-Islamic pride and boasting in ancestors and told people to stop boasting of their forefathers, since all are sons of Adam (Abu Dawud 5116).

defensive-wars-only.rationale: His first expeditions were caravan raids rather than defence (Watt, Muhammad at Medina, p. 231), and he later besieged and took Khaybar and its property (Ibn Ishaq, p. 515).

reviewHistory.rationale: Contested: Quran 2:190 limits fighting to those who fight you and 22:39 permits it to the wronged, while 9:29 and the campaigns against Khaybar, Mecca and Tabuk went beyond immediate defence.

arms-reduction.rationale: Quran 8:60 tells believers to prepare all the power and steeds of war they are able, not to reduce arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Quran 9:38-39 criticises those who hold back when called to fight; he expected obedience in his campaigns.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Quran 30:30 refers to the fitrah on which God created people and says no change should be in the creation of Allah; 4:119 treats altering it as Satan's command.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Contested: Quran 42:13 and 21:25 say all messengers brought the same message of one God, but 3:85 rejects any way other than Islam.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Quran 4:7 and 4:11-12 give women an inheritance share, but generally half of a male relative's. A right to inherit exists; equality of that right does not, so contested.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: No recorded position on sentencing repeat offenders; the fixed penalties in Quran 5:38 and 24:2 are about something nearby.

premarital-sex.rationale: He ordered unmarried people guilty of illicit intercourse flogged and exiled for a year (Bukhari 6831), and the Quran prescribes a hundred lashes for unmarried women and men alike.

reviewHistory.rationale: Quran 24:2 prescribes a hundred lashes for unmarried women and men guilty of sexual intercourse, and 17:32 says not to approach unlawful sexual intercourse.

women-suffrage.rationale: Told that the Persians had crowned Khosrau's daughter, he said 'Such people as ruled by a lady will never be successful' (Bukhari 4425), rejecting women's equal right to hold the highest office.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Bukhari 2335: "He who cultivates land that does not belong to anybody is more rightful to own it."

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Quran 4:82 says it has no discrepancy and he proclaimed it as the word of God; its literal reading is qualified by 3:7 on clear and allegorical verses.

simple-living.rationale: He told Ibn 'Umar to 'be in this world as if you were a stranger or a traveler' (Bukhari 6416), while Quran 7:32 asks who has forbidden the adornment and good things God brought forth, so low.

equal-conscription.rationale: When 'A'isha asked to take part in jihad, he told her 'Your Jihad is the performance of Hajj' (Bukhari 2875): the duty to fight fell on men.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Quran 9:60 limits zakat to listed categories, first the poor and the needy, rather than paying it to everyone.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: When the wife of Thabit b. Qays asked to leave him without blaming his character, he had her return the garden given as her dower and told Thabit to divorce her (Bukhari 5273).

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Bukhari 7144 reports him saying a Muslim must obey the ruler unless ordered to disobey Allah, in which case one should not obey. Close but not the same as a law being void.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: He disapproved of the killing of a woman found dead after a raid, condemning the killing of women and children (Bukhari 3014), yet said of night raids that might hit them 'they are from them' (Bukhari 3012), so low.

destroy-worshipped-objects.rationale: On entering Mecca at its conquest he struck the 360 idols around the Ka'ba with a stick, saying 'Truth has come and Falsehood will neither start nor reappear' (Bukhari 4287).

religious-offensive-war.rationale: On the Tabuk expedition he brought Christian Ayla and the towns of Jarba and Adhruh under his protection in return for poll tax, and sent Khalid to seize the Christian ruler of Duma (Ibn Ishaq, p. 607).

human-decline-since-golden-age.rationale: Anas reported him saying that no time will come but the time following it will be worse (Bukhari 7068); the decline runs from his own age, not an ancient golden age, so low.

divinely-chosen-superior-people.rationale: Quran 49:13 says peoples and tribes were made to know one another and the noblest is the most righteous, though 3:110 calls the believers the best community raised for mankind, so low.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: As ruler he enforced religious morals by penalty, beating drunkards and flogging fornicators (Bukhari 6773, 6831).

humans-entitled-to-use-animals.rationale: He slaughtered two rams with his own hands as sacrifices (Bukhari 5558).

avoid-permanent-military-alliances.rationale: His covenant at Medina was a standing defensive alliance binding Muslims and Jewish clans to help one another against any attack (Ibn Ishaq, p. 233).

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: Asked twice to fix prices, he declined, saying he would pray instead and that it is God who makes prices low and high (Abu Dawud 3450).

one-spouse-at-a-time.rationale: He was married to nine wives at once (Bukhari 5068).

opposition-only-legal-channels.rationale: Of future rulers who would not follow his guidance, he said to listen to the ruler and obey 'even if your back is flogged and your wealth is snatched' (Muslim 4785 in this edition).

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: He paid the man who cupped him his wages, and Ibn 'Abbas adds that he would not have paid them had it been disliked (Bukhari 2279).

conquest-no-lawful-claim.rationale: When he conquered Khaybar its land became 'the property of Allah, His Apostle, and the Muslims', and the Jews stayed on it only as sharecroppers (Bukhari 2338).

torture-always-illegal.rationale: At Khaybar he ordered al-Zubayr to 'torture him until you extract what he has' when Kinana b. al-Rabi' would not reveal the rest of a treasure (Ibn Ishaq, p. 515).

ban-spanking.rationale: He said to command children to pray at seven and to beat them for it at ten (Abu Dawud 495).

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: He sent Mu'adh to Yemen with orders that zakat be taken from the wealthy and given to the poor (Bukhari 1395): a standing levy for the poor, not one to be cut. notes: The Quran is treated as his proclaimed words; hadith (Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud) and Ibn Ishaq's biography are later reports (tier 4) and capped at medium. sunnah.com was unreachable (Cloudflare challenge), so hadith text comes from the fawazahmed0 hadith-api edition; Muslim numbers are that edition's. Later pass 2026-11-09 (claude-opus-5-5), bringing the audit to rules 5: Wikipedia sources (s2, s3, s6-s8) replaced by the texts they cite: the Covenant of Medina and the Farewell Sermon from Ibn Ishaq (Guillaume trans.), the record from Bukhari and from Watt, Muhammad at Medina (1956). Record over words: where the reports record his acts (executions, the assassination of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, the expulsions, zakat collection, punishments for drinking and fornication, the order to kill an apostate at Mecca) the answer rests on them; Quranic verses answer only where no act is recorded. Themes searched in this pass: government (his powers in Medina, pledges, judging), world (Tabuk, Ayla treaty, Khaybar, alliances), economy (price fixing, wages, zakat, land), society (women in office and war, divorce, polygyny, children), and the candidate statements. Several verses and reports point in different directions on apostasy, blasphemy and war; those are answered 0 or low. Later jurists' rulings are not used. Modern institutions (parliaments, central banks, the UN, elections) have no counterpart in his record and stay null.
